headline: Every finite disconnected undirected positive-weight signed network has an exact balance-controlled semigroup limit, spectral rate, and full principal-minor and characteristic pseudoforest expansion
nonclaims: priority for structural balance, signed consensus, signed matrix-tree theorems, or forest expansions
that the n<=4 unit-weight exhaustive regression proves the arbitrary-size positive-weight theorem
extension to directed, time-varying, nonlinear, zero-weight, or negative-weight networks
that every principal minor is merely an ordinary rooted-tree count
a prime-orbit law, Euler product, root number, automorphy, target determinant, or Hilbert--Polya operator
external peer review, literature exhaustiveness, or an acceptance score

route_a.strongest_failure: Finite graph spectra and forest expansions do not provide a source-native prime-power orbit law or the target analytic object.
route_a.strongest_positive: The positive semidefinite generator has a canonical self-adjoint semigroup, exact forest determinants, and a balance-controlled projector.

theorem.balance_kernel: each balanced component contributes its signed switch vector; every unbalanced component contributes no kernel
theorem.characteristic_polynomial: det(lambda I+L)=sum_F 4^{u(F)}w(F)lambda^{t(F)} product over tree components T of |V(T)|
theorem.exact_rate: on (ker L)^perp, ||exp(-tL)-P||_2=exp(-gamma t), gamma=min positive eigenvalue of L
theorem.nullity: number of balanced connected components, isolated vertices included
theorem.principal_minor: det L[V\R]=sum_F 4^{u(F)} product_{e in F} w_e, with each component a one-root tree or a root-free negative unicycle
theorem.projector: P=sum over balanced C of s_C s_C^T/|C|
theorem.semigroup: exp(-tL) tends to P; balanced components reach signed consensus and unbalanced components tend to zero
